## Rays
A ray is just a straight line with a starting position $\vec{S}$ and a direction $\vec{D}$.

You can walk along the ray using the parameter $t$, which gives us the ray equation:

$$ \text{Position on Ray} = \vec{S} + t\vec{D}$$

## Ray-Sphere intersection
For a ray with start position $\vec{S}$ and direction $\vec{D}$ and a sphere with centre position $\vec{C}$ and radius $r$:

$$a = \vec{D}^2$$
$$b = 2 \vec{D} \cdot (\vec{S} - \vec{C})$$
$$c = (\vec{S} - \vec{C})^2 - r^2$$
    
Determine the number of intersections by using the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac$

if < 0 then no intersection, if = 0 then one intersection, if > 0 then two intersections

Finally find $t$ using the quadratic formula:

$$ t = \frac{-b \pm sqrt(\text{discriminant})}{2a}$$

## Ray-Infinitely Long Cylinder intersection
For an infinitely long cylinder with end cap centre positions $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$,
and radius $r$ we use this instead:

$$a = \vec{D}^2 - \left(\vec{D} \cdot \widehat{AB}\right)^2$$
$$b = 2\overrightarrow{AS} \cdot \vec{D} - 2\vec{D} \cdot \widehat{AB}(\widehat{AB} \cdot \overrightarrow{AS})$$
$$c = \overrightarrow{AS}^2 - \left(\overrightarrow{AS} \cdot \widehat{AB}\right)^2 - r^2$$

where $\overrightarrow{AS}$ is the vector from $\vec{A}$ to $\vec{S}$, and $\widehat{AB}$ is the normalized vector from $\vec{A}$ to $\vec{B}$.


Then use the quadratic formula like before!

## Ray-Cylinder intersection

Ok, say you've got an intersection with the really long cylinder. What about the end caps?

First check if you are outside the plane of end cap A:

$$ \vec{AP} \cdot \vec{AB} < 0$$

If that passes, then check if the ray is actually heading towards end cap A:

$$ \vec{D} \cdot \vec{AB} > 0 $$

If that passes, check where the ray hits the plane of end cap A:

$$ t = -\frac{\vec{AS}\cdot\vec{AB}}{\vec{D}\cdot{\vec{AB}}}$$

## Ray-Cylinder intersection

Use the $t$ parameter to find a point $\vec{Q}$ on the plane:

$$ \vec{Q} = \vec{S} + t\vec{D}$$

Finally check whether that's within the radius of the cylinder:

$$ \|\vec{AQ} \| \leq r$$

If all those checks worked, you hit end cap A! 

If not, rinse and repeat for end cap B (careful, the dot checks will look a bit different). 

And if you aren't outside the plane of end caps A or B, then it turns out the ray-infinite cylinder intersection was correct after all!
